 Panama 0 – 0 6:00 PM ET Curaçao Live Updated a few seconds ago Kick-off in 21 minutes Panama vs Curaçao LIVE, Latest Score, Goals and Concacaf Nations League Updates
 Follow Panama vs Curaçao live from Estadio Rommel Fernandez in Panama City: 2026 Concacaf Nations League lineups, goals, match stats and live score updates.
 Coverage by Esteban Monsalve Updated November 15, 2026, 5:38 pm ET ADVERTISEMENT
 6:00 PM ET Last update 5:38 PM ET 5:38 PM ET a few seconds ago How can it be defined
 It's likely to be a tough match, with Panama pressing from the start and Curaçao holding their own for as long as possible. If the home team doesn't score early, anxiety will start to work against them, and every lost ball in midfield will become a dangerous counter-attack. If Panama opens the scoring, Curaçao will have to push forward and leave gaps, and that's where Christiansen's team could find their rhythm.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 Follow VAVEL on Google 5:38 PM ET a minute ago Refereeing and game data
 The referee will be Mexican Marco Antonio Ortiz, with Christian Kiabek Espinosa and Michel Morales as assistant referees, and Jorge Camacho as the fourth official. In Panama, the match can be seen on Telemetro, RPC TV (Channel 4), and TVMAX (Channel 9), with streaming on Medcom GO and radio coverage on RPC. Outside of Panama, it can be followed on various Concacaf channels depending on the region.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:37 PM ET a minute ago What the record says
 Recent history favors Panama. Of the last three matches between the two teams, Chile won two and drew one, all with Christiansen as manager. One of those matches was a 2-1 victory on October 13, 2023, in Curaçao, in that year's Nations League, and another was a 0-0 draw on June 15, 2021, in the 2022 World Cup qualifiers. Thursday's 0-0 draw adds to that tally. But historical advantage is of little use if it isn't converted into goals, and that's precisely what the team has lacked in recent months.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:37 PM ET 2 minutes ago Curacao: the undefeated team that comes to defend and to strike.
 Dick Advocaat's team arrives with a track record that no longer surprises anyone in the region. They finished the group stage undefeated, qualified for the last World Cup (just like Panama), and in recent years have steadily gained ground in the knockout stages of CONCACAF tournaments. The Dutch coach, with all his experience, knows how to manage a series like this: withstand pressure first and then strike with speed.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:37 PM ET 2 minutes ago Christiansen and the obligation to win
 Panama's coach, the Spanish-Danish Thomas Christiansen, warned before the first leg that details and even the smallest mistakes would be costly, and the series has proven him right. He was without Daivis Murillo and Giovany Herbert in Willemstad. For the return leg, the likely starting eleven is as follows: Orlando Mosquera in goal; Michael Amir Murillo, Andrés Andrade, José Córdoba, and César Blackman in defense; Carlos Harvey, Cristian Martínez, Adalberto Carrasquilla, and José Luis Rodríguez in midfield; and Édgar Yoel Bárcenas and José Fajardo up front. Other players called up include Ismael Díaz, Víctor Griffith, Azarías Londoño, and Manuel Morán, providing options off the bench.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:36 PM ET 2 minutes ago How was the first leg in Willemstad?
 At the Ergilio Hato Stadium, Panama took the initiative from the start, but they ran into a hero in Eloy Room. The Curaçao goalkeeper stopped Carlos Harvey in the 65th minute, one of the visitors' best chances, and responded again in the 36th minute with a save from a well-worked team move finished off by Jorge Gutiérrez. Curaçao also had their opportunities: Tahith Chong hit the post, and the home side's through balls caused problems for the Panamanian defense.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:35 PM ET 3 minutes ago They have a lot at stake.
 The pressure is compounded by a detail the local press keeps repeating: Panama has gone eight matches without a win in regulation time. A victory would end that drought and secure their fourth consecutive Nations League finals appearance.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:35 PM ET 4 minutes ago What the regulations say and what it means
 If Panama wins, by any score, they advance. If they draw with goals, 1-1 or more, Curaçao advances on away goals. If the match ends 0-0, the series goes to extra time. In other words, La Roja has no room for error. Every minute of a draw benefits the visitors more than the home team.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:35 PM ET 4 minutes ago Recent meetings between Panamá and Curaçao
 Across their last 2 official clashes, per the Panamá vs Curaçao head-to-head record and match center , the balance stands at 1 win for Panamá, 1 draw and 0 wins for Curaçao:
 2026: Curaçao 0–0 Panamá
 2023: Curaçao 1–2 Panamá
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:34 PM ET 4 minutes ago Curaçao
 Curaçao is stronger than its size suggests. A World Cup team, it finished the group stage undefeated with three wins and a draw. In the first leg, according to Concacaf, they held firm, allowing Panama only six shots, the lowest record for Dick Advocaat's team in a match of this competition.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 5:18 PM ET 21 minutes ago Panama
 Panama had already secured its place in the quarterfinals directly due to its regional ranking, so it didn't have to go through the group stage. In the first leg, on Thursday in Willemstad, they controlled the game from the start and created several chances, but failed to score. Christiansen made changes in the second half, but it wasn't enough.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 4:49 PM ET an hour ago The quarter-finals picture
 The situation in the quarterfinals is very different in each series. The United States has a six-goal advantage over Haiti, Canada and Jamaica won their first-leg matches against Guatemala and Mexico, respectively, and the two teams that lost need to come from behind.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 4:21 PM ET an hour ago What's at stake
 Panama is looking to qualify for the fourth consecutive edition. Since the series is still tied, the winner today advances and the loser is eliminated. I couldn't find how a tie is broken, either in the press or in the regulations. Based on the rankings, Panama has the advantage of hosting the second leg of the series.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 3:53 PM ET 2 hours ago Rommel Fernández Gutiérrez Stadium
 The Rommel Fernández Gutiérrez Stadium, officially named the Rommel Fernández Gutiérrez Olympic Stadium, is Panama's national stadium and the largest in the country. Panamanians know it as "The Colossus of Juan Díaz," after the Panama City neighborhood where it is located, and it forms part of the Irving Saladino Sports City. It is owned by INDE (the Panamanian Sports Institute) and operated by the Panamanian Football Federation.
 It was inaugurated on February 6, 1970, as the Revolución Stadium. Built for the XI Central American and Caribbean Games, it originally had a capacity of approximately 22,000 people, and according to some accounts, it was financed with loans during the government of Omar Torrijos. Adjacent to it were built the Nuevo Panamá Gymnasium, now the Roberto Durán Arena, and the Patria Swimming Pool. The structural plans for the Sports City were drawn up by the Technological University of Panama.
 The current name was adopted in 1993, in honor of Rommel Fernández, the striker nicknamed "El Pánzer" (The Panzer) for his strength and aerial prowess. He was the great pioneer of Panamanian football in Europe, excelling at Tenerife in Spain, and died in a car accident in Albacete on May 6, 1993, at the age of 27. Today, he is remembered as the man who paved the way for other players from the country.

 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 3:00 PM ET 3 hours ago Series tied
 The series is tied 0-0. In the first leg, on Thursday, November 12, at the Ergilio Hato Stadium in Willemstad, the teams drew 0-0. According to Concacaf, Panama held Curaçao to just six shots, the lowest total for Dick Advocaat's team in a Nations League or 2026 World Cup match, and goalkeeper Eloy Room had to make six saves.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 3:00 PM ET 3 hours ago Two needs in one series
 Panama, coached by Thomas Christiansen, comes into this match after a draw and still without a win. Curaçao, on the other hand, is a team that qualified for the 2016 World Cup and, according to one source, arrives strengthened after a strong group stage performance.
